minutes.headline: Committee tentatively ranked its top 20 FY22 capital projects, turnout gear first; final list due after next meeting.
minutes.summary: The Capital Planning Committee talked through FY22 capital requests, treating the Collins Center score as a guide only, and set a tentative order of twenty projects. Carpets, the police records room, the Town Hall roof cost and the Ritter costs were held for more information. They agreed to meet again the following Tuesday to finalize before the January 12 deadline to hand the list to the town manager.

budget_items.what_was_said: A bond issue set aside money for turnout gear, but release by the governor is uncertain, so some members did not rank it first on that basis.

budget_items.topic: Police body cameras and cemetery engineering and ADA
budget_items.what_was_said: Both are being funded by grants, so they were not ranked.
The Vertex items include sealants, windows, roof and chimney. The roof figure dates from 2018 and members think the total is too low.

budget_items.topic: Ritter envelope and gutter projects swapped in for Ritter vertex year one
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager proposed swapping the interior-heavy project for the envelope and gutter projects.

budget_items.topic: Running total of top ranked projects
budget_items.what_was_said: The top ten were noted as about a million dollars, with the Flat Hill culvert construction a large part. Later the total was cited higher and no target number was known.
The DPW director considers it an imminent failure, with construction money in next year's capital.
Members thought it belongs in the facilities budget rather than capital.
Members recalled design money already spent; the project itself is large.
A pickup for the DPW director was discussed.
A member questioned the cost of building a records room.

decisions.decision: Turnout gear set as number one and bulletproof vests number two in the tentative ranking.
Tentative ranks 18 to 20: utility tractor, police records room, primary school classroom AC; other items left unranked.
Next meeting set for the following Tuesday (Jan 5) to review carpets, records room, Town Hall roof and Ritter costs and finalize.
The town manager will seek a more refined Town Hall repair number from the architect.
Damon will circulate the reordered ranking list.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee set a tentative ranking of twenty FY22 capital projects, with fire turnout gear first and bulletproof vests second.
Ranks 18 to 20 were tentatively set as the utility tractor, the police records room and primary school classroom air conditioning; other items stay unranked.
Carpets, the police records room, the Town Hall roof cost and the Ritter costs were held for more information.
The town manager will ask the architect for a more refined Town Hall repair number, since members think the 2018 roof figure is too low.
The committee will meet the following Tuesday, Jan 5, to finalize the list; no votes were taken.

why_it_matters: This ranking shapes which FY22 capital requests, such as safety gear, culverts and Town Hall repairs, go to the town manager and may later reach Town Meeting for funding votes that affect the tax bill.
